segments.t: In their Parisian apartment kitchen, Noemie Leclerc prepares a roast lamb for an important dinner. Seeking reassurance from Mathias, her culinary confidence is shattered when he casually mentions their guest is a militant vegetarian. Let's listen to their conversation in French first.
Regarde, cet agneau est vraiment parfait.
Tu crois que sa femme va m'aimer?
Elle va t'adorer, sans aucun doute.
Et Catherine, qu'aurait-elle préparé?
Arrête de te comparer à Catherine.
C'est toi que j'aime passionnément.
Tout va très bien se passer.
Quels sont ses centres d'intérêt?
Elle est très écolo et engagée.
C'est-à-dire? Donne-moi un exemple.
Elle défend les espèces menacées.
Elle combat la cruauté des abattoirs.
Tu me dis ça maintenant?
Mon beau rôti est foutu!
Let's examine the conversation line by line and explore the French expressions.
Regarde, cet agneau est vraiment parfait.
'Look, this lamb is truly perfect.' Noemie admires the roasted meat she cooked for the guests. The masculine noun 'lamb' designates lamb.
Tu crois que sa femme va m'aimer?
'Do you think his wife will like me?' Noemie reveals her nervous desire to make a great impression. The verb phrase 'va m'aimer' expresses near future.
Elle va t'adorer, sans aucun doute.
'She will adore you, without any doubt.' Mathias offers warm and unconditional encouragement. The prepositional phrase 'without' means without doubt.
Et Catherine, qu'aurait-elle préparé?
'And Catherine, what would she have prepared?' Noemie cannot help measuring herself against Mathias's ex-wife. The conditional verb 'aurait' expresses hypothesis.
Arrête de te comparer à Catherine.
'Stop comparing yourself to Catherine.' Mathias firmly urges Noemie to let go of old ghosts. The imperative 'stop' governs an infinitive verb.
C'est toi que j'aime passionnément.
'It is you that I love passionately.' Mathias reminds Noemie of his romantic devotion. The emphatic cleft sentence 'c'est toi que' highlights the object.
Tout va très bien se passer.
'Everything will go very well.' Mathias promises that the dinner will be a great success. The pronominal verb 'to unfold' means to unfold or happen.
Quels sont ses centres d'intérêt?
'What are her areas of interest?' Noemie prepares dinner conversation topics in advance. The plural noun phrase 'centres d'interet' means hobbies or interests.
Elle est très écolo et engagée.
'She is very pro-environment and committed.' Mathias shares background on the director's wife. The shortened colloquial adjective 'ecolo' means environmentalist.
C'est-à-dire? Donne-moi un exemple.
'That is to say? Give me an example.' Noemie asks for specific details on the guest's causes. The transitional expression 'c'est-a-dire' requests clarification.
Elle défend les espèces menacées.
'She defends endangered species.' Mathias describes the guest's passionate activism. The feminine noun 'espece' designates a biological species.
Elle combat la cruauté des abattoirs.
'She fights slaughterhouse cruelty.' Mathias casually mentions that she campaigns against meat production. The noun 'slaughterhouses' means slaughterhouse.
Tu me dis ça maintenant?
'You tell me that now?' Noemie is horrified that she cooked a meat feast for an animal activist. The adverb 'now' marks present urgency.
Mon beau rôti est foutu!

'My fine roast is ruined!' Noemie realizes with despair that her main dish cannot be served. The colloquial adjective 'ruined' means ruined or wasted. Now let's listen to the complete discussion once more to reinforce the vocabulary.

Noemie discovers at the very last second that her roasted lamb will offend their vegetarian dinner guest. Scrambling to save the evening, she and Mathias must improvise an emergency meat-free menu. Now let's listen to the scene one last time.
On peut encore commander des légumes!
